The notes app

Models

Database models for the notes app.

The app stores a single kind of object, Note, which represents one sticky note on the board.

class notes.models.Note(*args, **kwargs)[source]

A single sticky note.

Notes are ordered newest first by default.

Variables:

  • title – Short title of the note (maximum 255 characters).

  • content – Body text of the note.

  • created_at – Date and time the note was created. Set automatically when the note is first saved.

  • updated_at – Date and time the note was last modified. Updated automatically on every save.

get_absolute_url() → str[source]

Return the canonical URL for this note.

Returns:

The path of the note’s detail page, for example /notes/note/1/.

Return type:

str

Views

Views for the notes app.

Each view handles one step of the create, read, update and delete (CRUD) workflow for Note objects and renders a template from notes/templates/notes.

notes.views.note_list(request: HttpRequest) → HttpResponse[source]

Display a list of all sticky notes.

Parameters:

request (django.http.HttpRequest) – The incoming HTTP request.

Returns:

The rendered notes/note_list.html page.

Return type:

django.http.HttpResponse

notes.views.note_detail(request: HttpRequest, pk: int) → HttpResponse[source]

Display the details of a single note.

Parameters:

  • pk (int) – Primary key of the note to display.

Returns:

The rendered notes/note_detail.html page.

Return type:

django.http.HttpResponse

django.http.Http404 – If no note with the given pk exists.

notes.views.note_create(request: HttpRequest) → HttpResponse[source]

Create a new sticky note.

A GET request shows an empty form. A POST request validates the submitted data and, if it is valid, saves the note and redirects to its detail page. Invalid data re-displays the form with errors.

Parameters:

request (django.http.HttpRequest) – The incoming HTTP request.

Returns:

The rendered form, or a redirect to the new note.

Return type:

django.http.HttpResponse

notes.views.note_update(request: HttpRequest, pk: int) → HttpResponse[source]

Update an existing sticky note.

A GET request shows the form pre-filled with the note’s current values. A valid POST request saves the changes and redirects to the note’s detail page.

Parameters:

  • request (django.http.HttpRequest) – The incoming HTTP request.

  • pk (int) – Primary key of the note to edit.

Returns:

The rendered form, or a redirect to the updated note.

Return type:

django.http.HttpResponse

Raises:

django.http.Http404 – If no note with the given pk exists.

notes.views.note_delete(request: HttpRequest, pk: int) → HttpResponse[source]

Delete a sticky note after confirmation.

A GET request shows a confirmation page. Only a POST request deletes the note, after which the user is sent back to the note list.

Parameters:

  • request (django.http.HttpRequest) – The incoming HTTP request.

  • pk (int) – Primary key of the note to delete.

Returns:

The confirmation page, or a redirect to the note list.

Return type:

django.http.HttpResponse

Raises:

django.http.Http404 – If no note with the given pk exists.

Admin

Admin site configuration for the notes app.

class notes.admin.NoteAdmin(model, admin_site)[source]

Admin configuration for the Note model.

Shows the title and timestamps in the change list, allows searching by title or content, and lists the newest notes first.

URL patterns

URL patterns for the notes app.

All routes are namespaced under notes and are mounted at /notes/ by the project URL configuration:

  • "" – list all notes (notes:note_list)

  • note/new/ – create a note (notes:note_create)

  • note/<pk>/ – show one note (notes:note_detail)

  • note/<pk>/edit/ – edit a note (notes:note_update)

  • note/<pk>/delete/ – delete a note (notes:note_delete)
